name: Jezero Crater
terrain: Crater floor with ancient river delta, rocky outcrops
temperature_notes: Near-equatorial (18 deg N); large day-night swings typical of Mars
water_ice: Ancient lake and river delta ~3.5 billion years ago; clays and carbonates, but no confirmed easily accessible ice deposit at the site
hazards: Rocks and delta cliffs; dust; crater terrain is rougher than a plain
description: A 45 km crater that once held a lake. One of the best places to look for signs of ancient life, but not the easiest place to land or live.

name: Gale Crater
mission: Curiosity rover (NASA, landed 6 Aug 2012) - Bradbury Landing
terrain: Flat plain (Aeolis Palus) inside a large crater, with 5.5 km Mount Sharp nearby
temperature_notes: Near the equator (about 5 deg S), so relatively mild for Mars and good sunlight
water_ice: Probable ancient crater lake; lower layers of Mount Sharp contain minerals that indicate a wet history. Water is in minerals, not an ice deposit
hazards: Dust; sharp rocks that damaged Curiosity's wheels; steep terrain if heading toward Mount Sharp
description: A 154 km crater with a mountain of layered rock in the middle - like a history book of Mars' watery past. Flat landing area, rough exploring further out.

name: Elysium Planitia
terrain: Very flat, smooth lava plain - chosen specially for landing safety
temperature_notes: Near the equator (4.5 deg N). InSight site temperature range during its mission: about -100 C to -20 C
water_ice: Little surface water evidence; chosen to study Mars' interior (marsquakes and heat flow), not water
hazards: Dust build-up on solar panels (this ended the InSight mission); otherwise very few rocks
description: The flattest, safest car park on Mars. Boring on the surface, perfect for landing - but you would have to bring or find your water elsewhere.

name: Oxia Planum
terrain: Wide, low, relatively smooth clay-rich plain
temperature_notes: Near-equatorial (18 deg N), similar latitude to Jezero
water_ice: Extensive clay (phyllosilicate) rocks formed with ancient water; evidence of groundwater activity. Clays are a sign water was here for a long time
hazards: Wind-shaped ridges and ripples (transverse aeolian ridges) can slow travel; dust
description: A flat clay plain where water once sat for a long time - its clays may preserve signs of past life, and its flatness makes it attractive for a base.

name: Utopia Planitia
mission: Viking 2 lander (NASA, 1976) and Zhurong rover (China, 2021) - coords are the region centre
terrain: Huge flat northern plain, some rocky and scalloped ice-rich ground
temperature_notes: High latitude (about 47 deg N), so much colder and less sunlight than equatorial sites
water_ice: NASA found a large buried ice deposit here - about as much water as Lake Superior - buried under 1-10 m of soil
hazards: Extreme cold; ice-rich ground can be uneven (scalloped permafrost); rocks in places
description: Mars' biggest plain, with a hidden ocean of ice under the soil. Fantastic for water, hard on warmth and solar power.
